The elders always tell me not to rush out when the sky turns gray. I used to think they were just overly cautious... until I saw how fast the wind changes out there.
I'm fixing my net knots like the old masters taught me. If you don't double-knot the nylon, a big lapu-lapu will snap it in a second!
Kuya Tomas used to show me how to read the clouds. He'd point at the horizon and say, 'When the sea swallows the sun in red, stay on land.'
Sometimes I get impatient waiting for the morning tide. But looking at the shore now... I realize the ocean demands respect every single day.
My Lola warned me: 'Don't whistle at night near the water, or the Siyokoy might pull your anchor.' I laugh, but I still keep quiet at dusk!
